findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-prd.md:R1 + R2 + R9 + AC-9 — R1 specifies auto-fire from `specflow:develop` Phase F at the F.5 → F.6 boundary; R2 specifies the manual `/specflow:complete {task-id}` escape hatch as the alternate path; R9 + AC-9 specify that plain-mode re-invocation refuses on tasks with existing retros via an existence-check on the entry's retro fields. The interview's Round 1 resolution names both trigger paths as legitimate (line 37: 'Phase F auto-fires `specflow:complete` once per task after Verifier passes ... manual `/specflow:complete {task-id}` is the alternate escape-hatch path'). But the PRD does not specify what happens when the two trigger paths fire CONCURRENTLY on the same task-id: e.g. Phase F's auto-fire begins for task `003-complete-skill-T2` AND the user simultaneously runs `/specflow:complete 003-complete-skill-T2` from a different terminal session before the auto-fire's retro write completes. R9's existence-check protects against sequential double-invocation (path B starts after path A finished writing) but cannot protect against concurrent double-invocation (both paths read the entry, both see no retro fields, both proceed to write). The race window is small but not zero — retro Q&A is interactive (5 questions), so the human-typing window is plausibly 30-90 seconds, which is more than enough for a parallel CLI invocation to interleave. The result would be either two retros written to the same entry (overwriting each other's fields) or the `decision-log.md` elevation prompt firing twice (second user-confirm overwrites first user-confirm).
findings.claim: Cross-artefact ambiguity (concurrency coverage gap) — R9's existence-check is a TOCTOU race when the two legitimate trigger paths (R1 auto-fire, R2 manual CLI) fire on the same task-id concurrently. The binary 'has retro fields populated yet?' framing of AC-9 cannot detect an in-flight retro because the retro fields are not written until the retro Q&A completes. The Phase 1 precedent for soft mutual-exclusion in shipping skills is the per-task-id scratch directory convention (`admin/scratch/{task-id}/`); this PRD inherits the convention via Phase F's scratch usage but does not name a lock-file or in-flight marker that would let path B detect path A's in-flight retro before both write.
findings.proposed_change: Extend R9 (or add a new requirement R14) covering the concurrent-trigger case: 'When `specflow:develop` Phase F auto-fires the retro for a task AND the user concurrently invokes `/specflow:complete {task-id}` for the same task before the auto-fire completes, the second invocation detects the in-flight retro via a per-task lock file at `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` (created by whichever path starts first; removed atomically when that path completes successfully or surfaces a refusal). The second invocation refuses with the structured chat line: "Retro for `{task-id}` is in flight (started `{timestamp}`). Wait for it to complete, then use `--amend` if you have additions." Lock files older than 30 minutes are considered stale and ignored (covers crashed-orchestration cleanup).' Add a corresponding AC verifying the lock-file create/remove discipline and the stale-lock heuristic. This closes the TOCTOU window R9 leaves open and makes the dual-trigger-path contract honest about concurrent invocations — the goal's surface (d) (zero silent failures) requires the race to surface explicitly rather than producing silent corruption.
